title: Today in one sentence
text: The whole market ended almost flat, but money moved around: big AI companies like Meta (+3.4%) and Microsoft (+1.1%) went up, while chip makers like AMD (-2.3%), TSMC (-2.0%) and NVIDIA (-1.3%) went down.

title: Meta is close to its high
text: Meta rose 3.4% to $742.96 after showing a new AI model. It is now less than 5% below its highest price of the past year, and about 5% below what experts expect it to be worth in a year ($781). When a stock gets close to its target, there is less room left in the experts' guess.

title: Microsoft is making its own chip
text: Microsoft showed a chip called Maia 300 and plans to use it for its AI from 2027. That could mean buying fewer chips from NVIDIA over time. But TSMC is the factory that builds it, so TSMC still wins either way.

title: A busy week for news
text: Big banks report their results on Tuesday, the inflation report (how fast prices are rising) comes out Wednesday, and TSMC reports on Thursday. If inflation comes in high, expensive stocks like AMD can drop, because interest rates may stay high.

title: Lesson 2: What is a price target?
text: A price target is an expert's guess of what a stock could be worth in about 12 months. The consensus is the average of many experts' guesses. GE trades near $309 and experts expect about $410, which is 33% higher. AMD is already at its target ($594 vs $608). Targets change often and are often wrong, so use them as a clue, not a promise.

title: About the data
text: Expert price targets are available for NVDA, TSM, AMD, GOOGL, AMZN, MSFT, META, LMT and GE. For the others we only use price movements. Prices are from the close on Monday, October 12, 2026.
